insight: Both Matthew 6:33 and Luke 12:31 emphasize the continuous, diligent seeking of God's kingdom as the believer's highest priority, promising that material needs will be provided by God as a result. The Greek imperative 'ζητεῖτε' in both verses commands an ongoing pursuit of God's sovereign reign, distinguishing believers from those who anxiously seek worldly provisions. While Matthew explicitly includes seeking God's righteousness alongside the kingdom, Luke focuses on the kingdom itself, yet both affirm that 'all these things'—the necessities of life—will be added by God's gracious provision.
